# Lab 09: Human-in-the-Loop (Go)

*You are on the Go track. Other tracks: [.NET](../dotnet/F09-dotnet.md), [Python](../python/F09-python.md), [TypeScript](../typescript/F09-typescript.md). Lab overview: [F09-lab.md](../F09-lab.md).*

**The User Problem:** Feature 07 routed the inbox, so now a ranger stares at forty messages that all need replies. Most answers are boilerplate the ranger has typed a hundred times, and typing them eats the afternoon. The obvious move is to let the AI answer, and the obvious disaster is the AI telling a visitor that campfires are fine during a burn ban, on official park letterhead. The ranger's problem is drudgery; the park's problem is that full automation of outbound communication is how you end up apologizing publicly.

*A Challenge lab. Do it if you finished [Module 3](../../M3-overview.md)'s Recommended lab and want another, or skip it without guilt: you will have seen this feature demonstrated either way.*

- **Goal:** put a human between the model and the visitor. The model drafts, a ranger approves, edits, or rejects, every decision is logged, and emergencies never reach the model at all.
- **Input:** `data/inquiries.jsonl`, six inquiries routed by feature 07, with category and park doc; `data/snippets/`, the four excerpts they cite.
- **How:** the starter already loops over the six inquiries and sends each one to the chat model with a drafting prompt, no gate. `complete/` adds a policy table, a gate above the model call, a review prompt, an outbox, and an audit log.
- **Model:** `llama3.2`, local. No key.

## The Concept

This feature has no new model mechanics — it's chat completions, same as F01. The entire point is a piece of plain code: a policy table, checked *before* any HTTP request is built, that decides whether a message is even allowed to reach the model. In `complete/main.go`:

```go
func laneFor(category string) string {
    for _, p := range policy {
        if p.category == category {
            return p.lane
        }
    }
    return "human-only" // fails closed: an unknown category never gets a draft lane
}
```

```go
if lane == "human-only" {
    fmt.Println("  NO DRAFT. Policy routes this straight to a human. Paging dispatch.")
    logDecision(decisionsPath, decisionRecord{ /* draft: nil, final: nil */ })
    continue // no chat() call happens — the model never sees this message
}
```

The system prompt also tells the model to output `ESCALATE:` instead of drafting when it detects an emergency. That instruction is a *request*; the `lane == "human-only"` branch above is a *guarantee*, because it runs in code, before the excerpt is even read from disk, and cannot be talked out of it by clever phrasing in the message. I verified this distinction live while building this port: `go/starter` (no gate) sent the overdue-hiker emergency straight to the model, which drafted a warm, procedural reply asking Diane for "his starting point on the Highline Trail" and signed it "Trailhead Guides Ranger Desk" — exactly the documented failure mode. `go/complete` (gated) printed `NO DRAFT` for the same message and made zero HTTP requests for it. Both behaviors are load-bearing to see, not just the safe one — `starter/`'s output is the demonstration of why the gate exists.

A second, weaker backstop exists *after* the model call: if the model's own draft text starts with `ESCALATE`, the draft is discarded and logged, but never offered for approval. This exists for messages that arrive miscategorized. It is explicitly not the control — the hard gate above is.

Every step below is one thing to make the program do. `starter/` is the unsafe baseline: every draft goes straight out, nothing is logged. Edit it until it has all five things `complete/` has: a policy table, a gate, a review prompt, an outbox, and an audit log.

## Running

Two independent modules, no dependencies to fetch.

```bash
go run .                # starter/: sends every inquiry's draft straight out, unread and unlogged
```

From `complete/`:

```bash
go run .                              # review the queue: [a]pprove / [e]dit / [r]eject / [s]kip
go run . --policy                     # print the routing policy table and exit
go run . --auto-approve-dry-run       # non-interactive run for testing and CI
go run . ../../data/inquiries.jsonl   # any queue file works
go run . --outbox <dir> --decisions <file>   # redirect the side effects
```

### Step 0: Run the starter and watch it fail on the emergency

**Do:** run `starter/` as it is:

```bash
go run .
```

It sends the same system prompt and drafting template as `complete/`, with no gate and no logging:

```go
draft, err := chat([]chatMessage{
    {Role: "system", Content: systemPrompt},
    {Role: "user", Content: userMessage},
})
fmt.Printf("=== SENT to visitor · %s (%s) ===\n", inq.ID, inq.Category)
fmt.Println(strings.TrimSpace(draft))
```

**Check:** look at `inq-0013`'s output specifically (Diane, the overdue hiker's wife). The system prompt explicitly instructs the model to output `ESCALATE:` and nothing else for exactly this case. In three recorded runs across the other tracks — and again when I ran this Go port live — the model ignores that instruction and drafts a fluent, procedural-sounding reply instead. The program prints `All replies sent. Nobody read them. Nothing was logged.` This is the failure the rest of the lab exists to make structurally impossible.

### Step 1: Define the policy table

**Do:** a plain ordered list of `{category, lane}` pairs — not derived from the model, not a map (Go map iteration order is random, and the printed policy table needs a stable, readable order):

```go
var policy = []struct{ category, lane string }{
    {"trail-condition", "draft-for-approval"},
    {"permit", "draft-for-approval"},
    {"complaint", "draft-for-approval"},
    {"general", "draft-for-approval"},
    {"lost-and-found", "draft-for-approval"},
    {"emergency", "human-only"},
}
```

**Why:** the lane is chosen by what a wrong answer costs, not by how good the model is at the category. Everything reversible can be drafted; emergency is irreversible and stays human-only.

**Check:** `go run . --policy` prints the six-row table and exits without touching the queue file or Ollama.

### Step 2: The gate

**Do:** as shown above — `laneFor()` defaults an unrecognized category to `"human-only"` rather than to a draft lane, so a category added upstream fails closed. The `if lane == "human-only"` branch sits above the snippet load and the `chat()` call, in `main()`'s loop, and it `continue`s without either.

**Check:** run `complete/` against the shipped queue and confirm `inq-0013` prints `NO DRAFT. Policy routes this straight to a human. Paging dispatch.` and nothing else for that inquiry — no `drafting...`, no model output.

### Step 3: Draft, review, and act

**Do:** for lanes that pass the gate, load the cited snippet (or the literal string `(none on file for this message)` if there's no doc or the file's missing), send the drafting prompt, then check the draft for an `ESCALATE` prefix as the backstop layer. If it's clean, show `[a]pprove [e]dit [r]eject [s]kip` and read one line from stdin:

```go
switch key {
case "a":
    decision = "approved"
    final = &draftCopy
case "e":
    decision = "edited"
    edited := readEdited(stdin, draft) // multi-line input, terminated by a lone "."
    final = &edited
case "r":
    decision = "rejected"
default:
    decision = "skipped"
}
```

`readEdited` copies the draft in if the reviewer presses Enter on the first line, so editing means appending rather than retyping from scratch.

**Check:** approving writes the draft verbatim to `outbox/<id>.txt`; rejecting or skipping writes nothing.

### Step 4: Outbox and audit log

**Do:** when `final != nil`, write `*final + "\n"` to `outbox/<id>.txt`. Every decision — gated, escalated-by-model, or reviewed — appends one JSON line to `decisions.jsonl` with exact keys `at`, `inquiryId`, `category`, `lane`, `decision`, `reviewer`, `draft`, `final`, `editDistance`:

```go
type decisionRecord struct {
    At           string  `json:"at"`
    InquiryID    string  `json:"inquiryId"`
    Category     string  `json:"category"`
    Lane         string  `json:"lane"`
    Decision     string  `json:"decision"`
    Reviewer     string  `json:"reviewer"`
    Draft        *string `json:"draft"`
    Final        *string `json:"final"`
    EditDistance int     `json:"editDistance"`
}
```

`editDistance` is a standard two-row Levenshtein DP between `draft` and `final` (or between `draft` and `""` when nothing was queued) — logged so a promotion decision ("this category needs less review") has data behind it, not a feeling.

**Check — verified live while building this port**, running `complete/` with `--auto-approve-dry-run` against scratch `--outbox`/`--decisions` paths:
- `inq-0013`'s record: `"lane":"human-only","decision":"escalated","draft":null,"final":null,"editDistance":0` — exactly the gated shape, and no `inq-0013.txt` appeared in the outbox.
- The other five inquiries each drafted a reply citing the correct document and section (`GLAC-CL-2026-01, Section 4.1` for the Avalanche Lake bridge, `GLAC-BC-2025-04, Section 4.2` for the Sperry campfire question, etc.), were auto-approved, and landed in the outbox.
- Final summary line: `Queue done: 5 approved, 1 escalated`.

### Stretch goal

Reorder the escalation instruction to the top of the system prompt instead of the end, and re-run `starter/`-style (no gate) against `inq-0013`. **Check:** the model may now emit an `ESCALATE:` line — and then keep writing the reply anyway, or over-fire `ESCALATE` on ordinary trail-condition messages. This is the documented shape of prompt-only safety: moving the instruction around changes the failure mode, not whether there is one. The code-level gate in `complete/` is unaffected either way, which is the entire argument for having it.

## What Is in This Folder

- `data/inquiries.jsonl`: six inquiries drawn from feature 07's full inbox, already routed, each carrying its category and the park doc it needs.
- `data/snippets/`: the four park-doc excerpts the drafts cite, quoted with document and section numbers.
- `policy-worksheet.md`: the lane table to fill in, one row per feature 07 category.
- `expected-output.md`: real `llama3.2` drafts for all six inquiries, annotated with what a ranger should approve, edit, or reject and why, plus the reference policy and the emergency result.
